title: Bread, pita, wheat or cracked wheat

content.title: About
content.content: Bread, pita, whole wheat and cracked wheat are products derived from the wheat grain. Bread and pita are baked from dough, while whole wheat and cracked wheat are used as flour, grains or additives in dishes. They provide carbohydrates, dietary fiber, B‑vitamins and essential minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pita originates from the Mediterranean and Middle East; its characteristic pocket forms when baked at high temperature.
Whole wheat retains the bran and germ, making it more nutritious than refined white wheat.
Cracked wheat (bulgur) is a staple in dishes such as couscous, tabbouleh and various porridges.
Sourdough bread contains natural probiotics that may support digestion.
Wheat is one of the oldest cultivated crops, domesticated over 10,000 years ago.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Wheat products deliver sustained energy through slow‑release glucose.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain bread and cracked wheat provide soluble and insoluble fiber that supports gut health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat supplies thiamine, riboflavin, niacin and folate, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Iron, magnesium, phosphorus and zinc are present in wheat‑based foods, contributing to overall nutrition.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: Fiber and protein in whole‑grain bread help maintain a feeling of fullness longer.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Some individuals have wheat allergy or gluten intolerance, which can cause gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White bread and pita can raise blood sugar quickly, which may be problematic for people with diabetes.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Gluten can trigger celiac disease, an autoimmune condition requiring a strict gluten‑free diet.

items.title: Added ingredients
items.content: Certain breads may contain preservatives, added sugars or trans fats; checking the label is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bread and pita are ideal for sandwiches, dips and as a side to soups. Whole wheat can be used as flour for baking, and cracked wheat works well in porridges, salads, soups or as a grain side dish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bread and pita in a cool, dry place in a paper bag or bread box to keep the crust from drying out. Keep whole wheat and cracked wheat in an airtight container in the refrigerator or a dark, cool pantry to prevent mold and preserve flavor.
